correctness.rationale: The six-Weierstrass-point labelling yields exactly sixteen nodes and sixteen tropes and the full, equivariant 16-by-16 integer incidence matrix. Its design identity A A^t=4Id+2J proves the exponent-twelve bound via A(3A^t-J)=12Id. Right exactness of coinvariants gives the 16-by-32 matrix [A|P_sigma-Id], and all 720 S6 actions are checked to respect incidence. There are eleven conjugacy types, all exactly covered. For each type, exact integer Smith reduction determines every invariant factor; independent Hermite indices of [A|P_sigma-Id|mId] at m=2,3,4 reproduce 2- and 3-primary elementary-divisor counts. The coordinate-sum map proves a Z/3 factor survives, while a 4-primary factor persists in every case. The two equal-orbit profiles are checked on both node and trope actions; distinct squarefree sextic factorizations exhibit both patterns over every odd finite field. Computations were executed from the actual packaged standalone verifier path before this assessment. No statement about characteristic two or geometric cohomology is claimed.

originality.rationale: Ohashi and Gonzalez-Hernandez supply the six-point theta/Weierstrass incidence and Galois permutation action, but no eleven-case integral coinvariant table was found in the inspected sections. Ducey et al. compute a closely related ordinary 16-vertex square-rook graph Smith group; there is no induced Kummer S6 Frobenius action in their theorem. The published 60-column Goepel tetrad lattice and 10-by-15 Segre node-plane coinvariant calculation differ in objects and integral modules and cannot imply these Kummer 16-by-16 coinvariant presentations. Searches of the indexed mathematical record and the recoverable owned history show no identical or dominating formulation. This is a qualified novelty assessment, not proof of exhaustive world priority.

value.rationale: The genus-two Kummer node–trope configuration and its Frobenius action are canonical arithmetic-geometric data, making the integral incidence coinvariant group a natural exact invariant. The complete eleven-partition classification exposes stable order-three and order-four arithmetic torsion, while two explicit, fieldwise-realized Weierstrass splitting types have identical node and trope orbit profiles and even equal coinvariant cardinalities, but nonisomorphic group structures. This is an integral refinement of familiar geometric and finite-etale counts, not a routine normalization, arbitrary slice, or mere recomputation of a known table. No unproved application to a Brauer or Picard obstruction is claimed.
